title: South Plains Financial, Inc. Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results
summary: LUBBOCK, Texas, Oct. 22, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- South Plains Financial, Inc. (NASDAQ:SPFI) (“South Plains” or the “Company”), the parent company of City Bank (“City Bank” or the “Bank”), today reported its financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.
body_markdown:
[PDF Version](https://www.spfi.bank/node/10731/pdf)


LUBBOCK, Texas, Oct. 22, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- South Plains Financial, Inc. (NASDAQ:SPFI) (“South Plains” or the “Company”), the parent company of City Bank (“City Bank” or the “Bank”), today reported its financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.


**Third Quarter 2026 Highlights**


- Net income for the third quarter of 2026 was $20.8 million, compared to $19.0 million for the second quarter of 2026 and $16.3 million for the third quarter of 2025.


- Diluted earnings per share for the third quarter of 2026 was $1.06, compared to $0.96 for the second quarter of 2026 and $0.96 for the third quarter of 2025.


- Average cost of deposits for the third quarter of 2026 was 207 basis points, compared to 208 basis points for the second quarter of 2026 and 210 basis points for the third quarter of 2025.


- Net interest margin, on a tax-equivalent basis, was 4.00% for the third quarter of 2026, compared to 4.00% for the second quarter of 2026 and 4.05% for the third quarter of 2025.


- Return on average assets for the third quarter of 2026 was 1.53%, compared to 1.44% for the second quarter of 2026 and 1.47% for the third quarter of 2025.


- Tangible book value (non-GAAP) per share was $29.23 as of September 30, 2026, compared to $29.60 as of June 30, 2026 and $28.14 as of September 30, 2025.


- The consolidated total risk-based capital ratio, common equity tier 1 risk-based capital ratio, and tier 1 leverage ratio at September 30, 2026 were 16.61%, 14.20%, and 12.42%, respectively.


Curtis Griffith, South Plains’ Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, commented, “As I prepare to retire as Chief Executive Officer at the end of this year, I could not be prouder of what City Bank and South Plains have become. The strong results we delivered in the third quarter, including near-record earnings and solid organic loan growth, reflect the strength of our franchise and reinforce my confidence in the future of the Company. Our leadership transition reflects years of thoughtful planning, and I am confident that Cory and the rest of our experienced management team are well prepared to build on our success. I look forward to continuing my service as Chairman and helping guide the long-term strategy of the Company.”


Cory Newsom, South Plains’ President, added, “I am honored by the Board’s confidence in appointing me as South Plains’ next Chief Executive Officer and excited to build upon the strong foundation that our team has created. Our third quarter results reflect the investments that we have made to expand our lending platform across our high-growth Texas markets, with annualized loan growth accelerating to 6.3% during the quarter, consistent with our expectations. We believe our loan pipeline remains healthy, and we continue to see opportunities to recruit experienced bankers as industry consolidation creates disruption across our markets. With a strong balance sheet, stable profitability and attractive returns, we believe we are well positioned to continue growing the South Plains franchise, enhancing the long-term earning power of the Bank and creating value for our shareholders.”


**Results of Operations, Quarter Ended September 30, 2026**


**Net Interest Income**


Net interest income was $51.5 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $50.3 million for the second quarter of 2026 and $43.0 million for the third quarter of 2025. Net interest margin, calculated on a tax-equivalent basis, was 4.00% for the third quarter of 2026, compared to 4.00% for the second quarter of 2026 and 4.05% for the third quarter of 2025. The average yield on loans was 6.75% for the third quarter of 2026, compared to 6.81% for the second quarter of 2026 and 6.92% for the third quarter of 2025. The average cost of deposits was 207 basis points for the third quarter of 2026, which is 1 basis point lower than the second quarter of 2026 and 3 basis points lower than the third quarter of 2025.


Interest income was $76.4 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $75.0 million for the second quarter of 2026 and $64.5 million for the third quarter of 2025. Interest income in the third quarter of 2026 increased $1.4 million compared to the second quarter of 2026 and increased $11.9 million compared to the third quarter of 2025. The $1.4 million quarterly increase was mainly due to an increase of $53.4 million in average interest-bearing assets, while the year-over-year increase of $11.9 million was primarily due to the acquisition of BOH Holdings, Inc.’s (“BOH”) approximately $667 million of interest-earning assets in the second quarter of 2026 along with organic growth.


Interest expense was $24.9 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $24.7 million for the second quarter of 2026 and $21.5 million for the third quarter of 2025. Interest expense in the third quarter of 2026 increased $295 thousand compared to the second quarter of 2026 and increased $3.4 million compared to the third quarter of 2025. The year-over-year increase of $3.4 million was mainly attributable to the acquisition of BOH’s approximately $611 million of interest-bearing liabilities during the second quarter of 2026 along with organic growth.


**Noninterest Income and Noninterest Expense**


Noninterest income was $13.8 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $14.1 million for the second quarter of 2026 and $11.2 million for the third quarter of 2025. The decrease from the second quarter of 2026 was primarily due to a decrease of $568 thousand in bank card services and interchange revenue, mainly as a result of incentives received during the second quarter of 2026. The increase in noninterest income for the third quarter of 2026 as compared to the third quarter of 2025 was primarily due to an increase of $2.3 million in mortgage banking revenues, mainly as a result of the change in the fair value adjustment of the mortgage servicing rights assets – a write-up of $1.6 million in the third quarter of 2026 compared to a write-down of $925 thousand in the third quarter of 2025 – based on market interest rate changes during the respective quarters.


Noninterest expense was $38.1 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $39.9 million for the second quarter of 2026 and $33.0 million for the third quarter of 2025. The $1.8 million decrease from the second quarter of 2026 was primarily the result of a decrease of $1.1 million in personnel expenses, mainly as a result of $710 thousand of acquisition-related expenses in the second quarter and a decline of $326 thousand in mortgage commissions during the third quarter. There was also a decline in other noninterest expenses of $596 thousand, mainly due to $343 thousand in acquisition-related expenses in the second quarter of 2026. The $5.1 million increase in noninterest expense for the third quarter of 2026 as compared to the third quarter of 2025 was largely the result of an increase in core operating expenses from the BOH acquisition of approximately $2.5 million and annual salary adjustments.


**Loan Portfolio and Composition**


Loans held for investment were $3.83 billion as of September 30, 2026, compared to $3.77 billion as of June 30, 2026 and $3.05 billion as of September 30, 2025. The increase of $59.7 million, or 6.3% annualized, during the third quarter of 2026 as compared to the second quarter of 2026 occurred as a result of organic loan growth during the quarter. The organic growth was net of one early loan payoff of $25 million during the quarter, which was fully secured by the borrower’s deposit account. As of September 30, 2026, loans held for investment increased $777.6 million as compared to September 30, 2025, as a result of BOH acquisition-related growth of $631.9 million and organic growth during the period.


**Deposits and Borrowings**


Deposits totaled $4.66 billion as of September 30, 2026, compared to $4.64 billion as of June 30, 2026 and $3.88 billion as of September 30, 2025. Deposits increased by $20.1 million in the third quarter of 2026 from June 30, 2026. Deposits increased by $779.5 million at September 30, 2026 as compared to September 30, 2025. Noninterest-bearing deposits were $1.18 billion as of September 30, 2026, compared to $1.15 billion as of June 30, 2026 and $1.0 billion as of September 30, 2025. Noninterest-bearing deposits represented 25.3% of total deposits as of September 30, 2026. The year-over-year change in total deposits was due to $595.6 million in deposits acquired through the BOH acquisition and organic growth broadly across the deposit portfolio during the period.


**Asset Quality**


The Company recorded a provision for credit losses in the third quarter of 2026 of $830 thousand, compared to $350 thousand in the second quarter of 2026 and $500 thousand in the third quarter of 2025. The increase in provision for both comparisons was largely attributable to activity in the third quarter of 2026 which included higher net charge-offs and increased loan balances.


The ratio of allowance for credit losses to loans held for investment was 1.38% as of September 30, 2026, compared to 1.41% as of June 30, 2026 and 1.45% as of September 30, 2025.


The ratio of nonperforming assets to total assets was 0.31% as of September 30, 2026, compared to 0.19% as of June 30, 2026 and 0.26% as of September 30, 2025. Annualized net charge-offs were 0.13% for the third quarter of 2026, compared to 0.06% for the second quarter of 2026 and 0.16% for the third quarter of 2025.


**Capital**


Book value per share decreased to $33.04 at September 30, 2026, compared to $33.43 at June 30, 2026. The change was primarily driven by a decrease in accumulated other comprehensive income (“AOCI”) of $25.5 million, partially offset by $17.4 million of net income after dividends paid during the third quarter of 2026. The decrease in AOCI was attributed to the after-tax decrease in fair value of our securities available for sale, net of fair value hedges, as a result of increases in long-term market interest rates during the period. The ratio of tangible common equity to tangible assets (non-GAAP) declined 16 basis points to 10.32% at September 30, 2026.

**About South Plains Financial, Inc.**


South Plains is the bank holding company for City Bank, a Texas state-chartered bank headquartered in Lubbock, Texas. City Bank is one of the largest independent banks in West Texas and has additional banking operations in the Dallas, El Paso, Greater Houston, the Permian Basin, and College Station, Texas markets, and the Ruidoso, New Mexico market. South Plains provides a wide range of commercial and consumer financial services to small and medium-sized businesses and individuals in its market areas. Its principal business activities include commercial and retail banking, along with investment, trust and mortgage services. Please visit[https://www.spfi.bank](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=FxqA9avwrxv3XMslHlWRlZHrMHcv4Y3_NvnbtqjtTSC0SQV98w5fx-u9JdqO5t4CHPq-FAYVxC_WBsl6urBXWGWjrJ6NdlM0h9rmOfxuTV4=) for more information.


**Non-GAAP Financial Measures**


Some of the financial measures included in this press release are not measures of financial performance recognized in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles in the United States (“GAAP”). These non-GAAP financial measures include Tangible Book Value Per Share, Tangible Common Equity to Tangible Assets, and Pre-Tax, Pre-Provision Income. The Company believes these non-GAAP financial measures provide both management and investors a more complete understanding of the Company’s financial position and performance. These non-GAAP financial measures are supplemental and are not a substitute for any analysis based on GAAP financial measures.


We classify a financial measure as being a non-GAAP financial measure if that financial measure excludes or includes amounts, or is subject to adjustments that have the effect of excluding or including amounts, that are included or excluded, as the case may be, in the most directly comparable measure calculated and presented in accordance with GAAP as in effect from time to time in the United States in our statements of income, balance sheets or statements of cash flows. Not all companies use the same calculation of these measures; therefore, this presentation may not be comparable to other similarly titled measures as presented by other companies.


A reconciliation of non-GAAP financial measures to GAAP financial measures is provided at the end of this press release.
